investigations.title: Shared package bootstrap boundary and ownership
investigations.question: Can @mindroom/common be bootstrapped at the frozen target with a coherent workspace boundary, build contract, and unambiguous capability ownership before any Codebase mutation?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: The bootstrap task is a prerequisite for all Wave 0 tasks and the wider implementation graph; an incorrect package boundary or capability owner would contaminate every downstream task and its receipts.
acceptanceCriteria: The active Yarn workspace topology discovers Codebase/packages/common/mindroom without a root workspace-pattern change.
The pinned AFFiNE reference and active Codebase agree on the relevant Yarn, Node, and packages/common topology.
The planned package path and @mindroom/common name have no active or pinned-reference collision.
The package can remain isolated from @affine/core and renderer-only dependencies using existing repository conventions.
The frozen capability owner, contract, acceptance test, queue entry, and downstream dependency evidence identify one coherent bootstrap scope.
No proof step modifies Codebase.
investigations.decision: COMPLETE. Authorized change control resolved MR-IMPL-BOOTSTRAP-001 to the single canonical owner MR-CAP-001, retained MR-IMPL-160 as MR-CAP-160's primary task, migrated current backup authority to a verified immutable GitHub tag, and returned full frozen certification plus Step 11b to PASS without Codebase mutation.
investigations.notes: The original invocation correctly stopped on two blockers. Both are preserved in lifecycle evidence as DISCOVERED, CHANGE_CONTROL_AUTHORIZED, and RESOLVED. Wave 0 remains READY_NOT_STARTED; MR-INV-002 was not begun.

changeControlLifecycle.meaning: Original MR-INV-001 invocation proved the contradiction and missing active laptop backup.

investigations.title: Wave 0 application architecture preservation boundary
investigations.question: Which application entrypoints, package boundaries, and registrations must Wave 0 preserve, and which exact changes are actually required by MR-IMPL-001?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: MR-IMPL-001 unlocks Electron main, renderer, preload, testing, performance, office, and runtime-bundling work; an overbroad architecture edit would violate the KEEP contract.
acceptanceCriteria: All active application entrypoints and runtime registrations mapped to MR-CAP-001 are verified against Codebase.
Required Wave 0 mutations are separated from already-correct preserved behavior.
Allowed, generated, and forbidden paths are reconciled with the actual build graph.
No unresolved architecture ownership ambiguity remains.
investigations.decision: Fifth key-aware change control passed 224/224 checks, 120/120 challenges, Step 11b, 47-vs-47 independent discovery equality, and exactly one fresh independent review (VERIFIED). All 4/4 criteria pass; MR-BLOCK-003 is resolved.
investigations.notes: Attempts 1-4 remain truthful failed history on non-authoritative WIP branches. Attempt 5 generically inspects dictionary keys and values, covers CAPABILITY_TO_PATH_MAP, FOLDER_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX, and PUBLIC_ENTRYPOINT_PLAN, fails closed on unknown keyed authority, preserves Codebase, and stops before MR-INV-003/Wave 0.

thirdChangeControl.reviewDefect: Manual discovery omitted PUBLIC_ENTRYPOINT_PLAN; stale temporary authority was not rejected.

fourthChangeControl.reviewDefect: Dictionary keys were not treated as authority identities; CAPABILITY_TO_PATH_MAP and FOLDER_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX were missed.

fifthChangeControl.references: 3149/3149 classified and validated at reviewed gate

investigations.title: Electron main, preload, renderer, and IPC trust boundaries
investigations.question: What are the actual Electron process, privilege, preload exposure, and IPC registration boundaries that Wave 0 must preserve or constrain?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: Privileged filesystem and credential operations must remain outside the renderer, and the three tasks have explicit dependency order and security invariants.
acceptanceCriteria: BrowserWindow security settings and runtime process owners are proven from Codebase.
Every preload exposure and corresponding main-process handler family is mapped.
Renderer access to privileged operations is classified and bounded.
No unresolved IPC or security architecture risk remains before mutation.
investigations.decision: Wave 0 must preserve the current context-isolated Electron preload/IPC/security boundaries exactly; no frozen-plan change is required.
investigations.notes: Tightly couples MR-IMPL-002, MR-IMPL-003, and MR-IMPL-004 because separating the bridge endpoints from their process owners would make the evidence incomplete.

investigations.title: BlockSuite and page-mode integration surface
investigations.question: Which BlockSuite packages, editor specs, registrations, and page-mode APIs are the compatible preserved foundation for Wave 0?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: MR-IMPL-005 is the prerequisite for page mode and multiple Wave 1 editing/canvas capabilities; version or API mistakes would invalidate downstream work.
acceptanceCriteria: Active BlockSuite package versions and workspace boundaries are identified.
Page editor construction and spec registration paths are proven from Codebase.
AI-specific adjacent paths are separated from the non-AI foundation.
The KEEP decision is compatible with the pinned AFFiNE reference and licensing boundary.
investigations.decision: Wave 0 must preserve the active BlockSuite 0.27.0 workspace family and existing ViewExtensionManager page-spec pipeline. The KEEP decision is compatible with the pinned AFFiNE reference and MIT-scoped BlockSuite licence boundary.
investigations.notes: Derived from the MR-CAP-005 -> MR-CAP-006 dependency and the critical graph risk on both capabilities.

investigations.title: Wave 0 local-first and offline sequencing
investigations.question: Can Wave 0 satisfy its no-cloud, no-telemetry, offline-capable invariants while local-only network enforcement is scheduled in Wave 1?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: The active AFFiNE-derived shell contains cloud-adjacent systems, while every Wave 0 contract asserts local-only behavior; a sequencing contradiction would block Wave 0 completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Boot-time and core-path network dependencies are enumerated from actual registrations.
Optional/deferred network adapters are separated from mandatory runtime paths.
Wave 0 gate criteria are reconciled with MR-IMPL-099's Wave 1 placement.
No unresolved offline-first sequencing contradiction remains.
investigations.decision: Wave 0 preservation/verification is compatible with local-only network enforcement remaining in Wave 1; no frozen-plan change is required.
investigations.notes: Derived from explicit Wave 0 invariants and the frozen placement of local-only network enforcement in Wave 1.

investigations.title: Wave 0 toolchain and cross-platform build compatibility
investigations.question: Are the pinned Node, Yarn, TypeScript, Electron, native-module, and platform command assumptions available and mutually compatible for Wave 0 verification?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: The active default Node v24.18.0 is outside the repository's >=22.12.0 <23.0.0 engine range and .nvmrc pins 22.23.1; execution must not begin with an unsupported toolchain.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact supported runtime and package-manager versions are proven from repository files.
A compatible Node runtime is available or a deterministic pre-Wave-0 setup action is established.
Wave 0 build and test commands are portable or have explicit platform-specific owners.
Native/Electron module compatibility has no unresolved hard blocker.
investigations.decision: Wave 0 is toolchain-compatible after a deterministic pre-flight setup: use Node 22.23.1 and invoke vendored Yarn 4.13.0 with node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.13.0.cjs. No Codebase change or frozen-plan change is required.
investigations.notes: The runtime mismatch was observed during MR-INV-001 but is intentionally left for this separate investigation.

investigations.title: Wave 0 test harness and release-gate evidence
investigations.question: Can all 13 Wave 0 acceptance tests and VERIFY_WAVE_0_RECEIPT be executed with real repository commands and evidence without inventing a test harness?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: GATE-WAVE_0 cannot pass on mapped test names alone; command ownership, fixtures, negative checks, and receipt production must be known before mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Wave 0 test ID maps to an executable repository-discovered command and owner.
Required fixtures and offline/cross-platform conditions are available or explicitly implementation-bound.
Receipt format and independent review responsibility are unambiguous.
No release-gate prerequisite is impossible before Wave 0 completion.
investigations.notes: The frozen matrix currently has 7 Wave 0 tasks, 13 tests, and one wave receipt.

investigations.title: Pinned AFFiNE parity, transplant, and licence boundary
investigations.question: Do Wave 0 KEEP/ADAPT decisions rely only on legally usable, pinned AFFiNE/BlockSuite evidence, and does any task require a transplant-vs-invention receipt before code?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: Every Wave 0 task requires pinned-reference searches, and restricted backend/native or embedded third-party scopes cannot be copied by assumption.
acceptanceCriteria: The pinned upstream commit/tree/archive evidence is verified from the frozen repository.
Active-vs-reference deltas are classified for all Wave 0 target families.
MIT, mixed AFFiNE EE/MPL, and embedded third-party boundaries are separated.
Every transplant or invention decision required before Wave 0 is either approved or proven unnecessary.
investigations.notes: Restricted backend/native scopes are relevant to architecture and Electron boundaries even when the initial decision is KEEP_EXISTING.

investigations.title: Wave 0 execution order and rollback checkpoints
investigations.question: What exact Wave 0 micro-batch order and reversible checkpoints satisfy the frozen dependency graph without mixing independent implementation tasks?
investigations.whyRequiredBeforeCode: The bootstrap is audited as a prerequisite to every Wave 0 task, while Electron and page-mode tasks have additional same-wave dependencies; rollback must preserve the frozen Codebase baseline and user data.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic topological order exists for all seven Wave 0 tasks.
Parallel-safe and strictly sequential task boundaries are identified.
Each micro-batch has scoped pre/post hashes, tests, receipts, and rollback actions.
No same-wave ordering artifact contradicts the canonical task dependency audit.
investigations.notes: Derived from the canonical dependency audit, which makes the bootstrap a prerequisite of all six primary Wave 0 tasks.
